ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $BC=120$, the height $AD=60$, and square $EFGH$ has one side on $BC$, with points $E$, $F$ respectively on $AB$, $AC$, and $AD$ intersects $EF$ at point $N$. What is the length of $AN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the side length EF=EH=x of the square EFGH, \\
$\because$ EFGH is a square, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$HEF=$\angle$EHG=90$^\circ$, EF$\parallel$BC, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$AEF$\sim$ $\triangle$ABC, \\
$\because$ AD is the altitude of $\triangle$ABC, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$HDN=90$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ the quadrilateral EHDN is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$ DN=EH=x, \\
$\because$ $\triangle$AEF$\sim$ $\triangle$ABC, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AN}{AD}=\frac{EF}{BC}$, \\
$\because$ BC=120, AD=60, \\
$\therefore$ AN=60−x, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{60−x}{60}=\frac{x}{120}$, \\
Solving for x, we get: x=40, \\
$\therefore$ AN=60−x=60−40=\boxed{20}.

因为 EF 也是正方形边长，所以 s=120(1-s/60)。解得 s=120-2s，即 3s=120，所以 s=40。

AN 是从 A 的高度 60 到 EF 的高度 s=40 的竖直距离，因此 AN=60-40=20。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $BC=120$, the height $AD=60$, and square $EFGH$ has one side on $BC$, with points $E$, $F$ respectively on $AB$, $AC$, and $AD$ intersects $EF$ at point $N$. What is the length of $AN$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the side length $EF=EH=x$ of the square $EFGH$. \\
$\because$ $EFGH$ is a square, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle HEF=\angle EHG=90^\circ$, and $EF\parallel BC$. \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AEF\sim\triangle ABC$. \\
$\because$ $AD$ is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle HDN=90^\circ$. \\
$\therefore$ the quadrilateral $EHDN$ is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$ $DN=EH=x$. \\
$\because$ $\triangle AEF\sim\triangle ABC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AN}{AD}=\frac{EF}{BC}$. \\
$\because$ $BC=120$ and $AD=60$, \\
$\therefore$ $AN=60-x$. \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{60-x}{60}=\frac{x}{120}$. \\
Solving for $x$, we get $x=40$. \\
$\therefore$ $AN=60-x=60-40=\boxed{20}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, base BC is horizontal, A is above; AD goes from A perpendicular to base BC, with foot D. Square EFGH is located inside the triangle, base HG lies on BC, top side EF is parallel to BC; E is on AB, F is on AC; AD intersects EF at N. The problem gives BC=120, AD=60.
Reasoning: Let y=AN. Because EF is parallel to BC, triangle AEF and triangle ABC are similar. Thus EF/BC=AN/AD, that is EF/120=y/60, so EF=2y. Also because EFGH is a square, side length EF equals the perpendicular distance from EF to BC; on height AD, this distance is DN=AD-AN=60-y, so EF=60-y. The two equations are equal: 2y=60-y, obtaining 3y=60, therefore y=20. So AN=20.
